title: Review of ringswim c2 (S,I,B,M): swimming walled cells replicate on fresh seeds 3 and 4, but the L ring sits at the 1.5 threshold (1.50-1.52; author 1.27-1.59) with a third of cells not membrane-like (Weak)
summary: Looked at the claim's sheets, radial plots and strips, then ran world_claim.py on fresh seeds 3 and 4 and world_chi0.py on seed 3 (claim protocol, --spf 100, T=20000). From noise, walled cells form by t=800 and move as crescents with a depletion wake on both seeds (rerun/seed3/sheet.png, tracks.png #464 and #429 swimming crescents t=13800-18300); labkit finds 8 and 7 long-lived tracks moving >= 1 body length, max 3.8 and 5.7 BL. The L ring (labkit aggregate radial, rim/core) is 1.52 (43/62 individuals membrane-like) and 1.50 (38/60) against 1.13 (0/131) with chi=0, so the ring is real and chi-dependent but at the rubric's 1.5 bar, and across the five seeds now run it spans 1.27-1.59. In the crops the yellow link is often concentrated on one side of a crescent rather than all round. I tried a per-cell ring split by speed but my mask included the wall halo and the measure was inconclusive, so I cannot say whether moving cells keep a full ring.

observations.S: rerun/seed3/sheet.png t=0: noise over the whole domain
observations.I: rerun/seed3/sheet.png t=800-20000: discrete walled cells, 5-12 at a time
observations.B: numbers.txt: L rim/core 1.52 and 1.50 (seeds 3, 4) vs 1.13 for chi=0 (rerun_chi0/seed3)
observations.M: rerun/seed3/tracks.png #464, #429 crescents moving t=13800-18300; numbers.txt max 3.8 and 5.7 BL

not_checked: ring on moving cells specifically (my per-cell measure failed)
verdicts.limitation: The ring is chi-dependent but only at the 1.5 bar on average, about a third of individuals are not membrane-like, and in crescents the link sits on one side; I could not confirm that the swimming individuals are the ringed ones, so same_individuals is false.
